description: Electric utilities, co-ops, municipal utilities and retail electric providers
coverage_notes:
[electric-great-lakes] COMPLETENESS: Checked against EIA-861 2024 (rosters/electric_utilities.csv): all 663 state-rows for OH/MI/IN/IL/WI collapsed to 577 distinct billers (574 after reviewer merges, see below) here (utilities serving several states, e.g. Indiana Michigan Power, NSP-Wisconsin, WEC, and suppliers active in both OH and IL, are merged into one entry with multiple service_area states). Only three EIA rows were deliberately excluded because they have no residential billing (University of Illinois - 1 customer; Ohio Valley Electric Corp - 1; AGC Division of APGI - 2). DETAILED TIER (78): all 30 residential-serving investor-owned utilities (Westfield Electric Co. is covered by the Pioneer Power & Light/Westfield Milling entry and kept as a roster row; Consolidated Water Power Co., 91 mostly industrial customers, is roster only), all 29 cooperatives/municipals with >25,000 customers, and the 19 largest retail suppliers (>=20k customers). Most detailed entries were verified by fetching the official pages this session (curl + text extraction); entries marked verified=false (ComEd - JS-only site; Naperville, SCI REMC, Northeastern REMC - sites block automated fetch) rely on search-result URLs. Phone numbers for CEI, Toledo Edison, Duke Energy Ohio, AES Ohio and ComEd were cross-checked on Dynegy's utility contact directory. ROSTER TIER: identity, EIA ID, customers, and website/phone only where HIFLD 2022 attributes had one (about 46 of 499 roster rows); HIFLD websites for Ohio co-ops were found shifted between rows, so every HIFLD website was re-fetched and 30 were corrected, confirmed or removed (see per-entry notes). TVA: no TVA distributors operate in these five states. RETAIL SUPPLIERS: in OH and IL, supplier charges are normally on the utility's consolidated bill, so the utility entries are the pay-bill path; supplier entries give contact/help info. KEY GAPS: (1) ~350 roster co-ops/municipals (mostly <25k customers; ~290 small municipal systems) have no website recorded - state association directories (Indiana Electric Cooperatives, Ohio's Electric Cooperatives, MECA, AIEC, WECA, AMP, IMPA, IMEA, WPPI, MPPA, MEUW) are JS-rendered or blocked and were not parsed; (2) most municipal bills are combined city utility bills (water/sewer/trash) - see the water category; (3) WebSearch budget was exhausted mid-run, so ~80 roster retail suppliers and some mid-size co-ops (e.g. Harrison REMC, Kankakee Valley REMC, Polk-Burnett, Jo-Carroll, Norris, Riverland, NineStar Connect, WIN Energy/Western Indiana, Heartland REMC, Manitowoc PU, Sun Prairie, Richmond Power & Light, Columbus OH DPU, Westerville) need a second pass; (4) Duke Energy and CenterPoint pages render phones client-side - numbers noted as published but not all text-confirmed; (5) EIA-861 2024 does not reflect 2025-26 mergers/rebrands beyond those noted (e.g. Energy Harbor->Vistra, Palmco->Indra). || REVIEWER PASS (2026-09-29): (a) Completeness re-checked by EIA utility ID: every OH/MI/IN/IL/WI EIA-861 2024 row except the 3 non-residential rows above is represented. Merged duplicates: XOOM Energy Ohio + XOOM Energy Illinois (one NRG brand), StateWise Energy Ohio + Illinois, Westfield Electric Co. into the Pioneer Power & Light/Westfield entry -> 574 entries. (b) Upgraded 50 roster entries to detailed (every co-op/municipal with ~11k-25k customers that has a reachable website, plus Public Power LLC): Harrison REMC, Polk-Burnett, Kankakee Valley REMC, Richmond P&L, Norris, JCE Co-op (Jo-Carroll), Riverland, WIN Energy REMC, Barron, Consolidated (OH), Boone Power, Kosciusko REMC, NineStar Connect, Oakdale, Sun Prairie, Heartland REMC, Manitowoc PU, Holmes-Wayne, Pioneer (OH), Guernsey-Muskingum, Marquette BLP, Lorain-Medina, Kaukauna, Tri-County (IL), Carroll White REMC, Grand Haven BLP, RushShelby, Scenic Rivers, Bay City, Dubois REC, Marshfield, Paulding Putnam, Hancock-Wood, Eastern Illini, Logansport, Wyandotte, Eau Claire Energy, Parke REMC, Thumb Electric, Whitewater Valley, Bartholomew REMC, St. Croix, Carroll (OH), Butler Rural, Noble REMC, Vernon, Southern Illinois, Midwest Electric (OH), Traverse City L&P. Detailed = 128 (30 IOUs, 58 co-ops, 20 municipals, 20 retail suppliers). (c) The 4 previously unverified entries (ComEd, Naperville, SCI REMC, Northeastern REMC) were rendered/fetched and are now verified=true; ComEd links were replaced with the real sub-pages (automatic-payment, paperless-ebill, pay-by-mail-phone, payment-assistance). Filled missing statements_history/paperless/view_bill for Consumers, Ameren IL, We Energies, WPS, UMERC, Duke IN/OH, I&M, Alliant, CEI, Toledo Edison, MidAmerican, UPPCO, MGE, CPP, AES OH/IN; Xcel NSP-W links now point at the my.xcelenergy.com pages the old URLs redirect to (JS-rendered; only HTTP status confirmed). Fixed HomeWorks links pointing at a dead staging host, a 404 Barron PDF, and corrected pay-by-phone numbers for MGE, Northeastern REMC, Lansing BWL. All ~500 URLs on detailed entries were HTTP-checked; remaining non-200s are bot challenges (Corn Belt, SE Illinois Electric, CleanChoice help center, Naperville, SCI REMC, NREMC) that were confirmed through WebFetch/browser. (d) Senior programs: found utility-specific senior benefits - Consumers Energy Senior Citizen Bill Credit ($4/mo), CWLP income-qualified 10% Senior Citizen Discount (age 62+), Michigan Winter Protection for 65+ at Cherryland/PIE&G/Thumb/Traverse City L&P, ComEd/Duke/WEC third-party notification. Where the utility page listed nothing, senior_programs is marked 'General state programs (not listed on the utility page reviewed)'. (e) Websites: added fetched-and-title-matched websites for ~130 more roster co-ops, municipals and retail suppliers (291 of 574 entries now have a website); 16 were set from known domains whose servers block automated fetches (noted per entry). Supplier rebrands noted from domain redirects: Titan Gas -> CleanSky Energy, RPA Energy -> Green Choice Energy, Direct Energy Business -> NRG. REMAINING GAPS: ~280 entries (mostly municipal systems under 5k customers and small suppliers) still have no website; Energy Services Providers, Inc. (45.7k IL/OH customers) brand still unconfirmed (its presumed Ohio/Illinois Gas & Electric sites are parked); Rock Energy Cooperative (18k), Western Indiana Energy REMC (17k), Wayne-White, Orange County REMC, Jay County REMC, Wisconsin Rapids WW&L, Shawano, Columbus OH, Westerville, St. Charles IL and Union Rural Electric were not upgraded (site unreachable or bot-blocked). The web-search tool budget was already exhausted, so reviewer discovery relied on sitemaps, on-site link crawling and verified domain probes. || ROSTER BACKFILL 2026-09-30 (task roster-backfill-electric-great-lakes, done in place): (1) Municipal/co-op websites: 226 municipal and co-op roster rows had no website (216 municipal: OH 60, WI 60, IN 54, IL 28, MI 14, plus 10 co-ops). 185 now have one: 8 co-ops (Rock Energy rock.coop, Wayne-White waynewhitecoop.com, Jay County jayremc.com, McDonough mcdonoughpower.com, Spoon River srecoop.org, Newton County REMC newtoncountyremc.com, Washington Island wiecoop.com, Wolverine Power Marketing) and 177 municipals. Sources were the AMP, MEUW and WECA member directories, the Touchstone locator, the CISA .gov list, and name-pattern domain probes. Each homepage was fetched and accepted only when the page named the town and state, or for script-rendered pages when the title named the town. Sites behind JS or Cloudflare challenges were opened in a real browser. Rejected look-alikes: Town of Arcadia vs City of Arcadia WI; Town of Orion and Town of Clearfield found through .gov city-field matches; Town of Mazomanie vs the Village; cityofripley.org (Ripley WV); thevillageofviola.org (Viola IL); stale MEUW links now parked or hijacked (belmontwi.com, newlisbon.net); parked domains (knightstown.org, glouster.com, roodhouse.com, hagerstownindiana.com, auburnin.com). 136 roster municipal/co-op rows now carry a pay_bill link taken from the site's own navigation, with the processor recorded (Invoice Cloud, Paymentus, Payment Service Network, Municipal Online Payments, Paygov.us, BS&A Online, Community Connect, GovPayNow, MerchantTransact, NISC SmartHub). Many also have autopay forms and energy-assistance pages. Still missing (41): Western Indiana Energy REMC (17k customers; no site found) and Orange County REMC (IN), plus 39 small municipals, mostly under 1,000 customers (IN 15, IL 10, OH 8, WI 4, MI 2). Two of them have sites that block automated checks: Clintonville WI and Mascoutah IL. (2) Detailed upgrades: all 28 roster municipal/co-op utilities with 10,000 or more customers that have a findable site were upgraded to detailed (Columbus Water & Power, Buckeye REC, Rock Energy, Westerville, St. Charles, Egyptian EC, Bowling Green, Wisconsin Rapids WW&LC, Wadsworth, Wayne-White, Greenfield IN, Niles, Painesville, Union Rural EC, Batavia, Oconomowoc, Menard EC, Piqua, Dunn Energy, Peru Utilities, Washington EC, Oconto EC, Alger-Delta, Illinois EC, Geneva, Crawfordsville EL&P, Jump River, Shelby EC). They now carry pay, autopay, history, paperless and assistance pages, phones, pay-by-phone numbers and processors where published. Senior-specific benefits found: Piqua's 5% Senior & Disabled Citizen Discount (age 62+, income-qualified) and Columbus programs for seniors 60+. Website corrections: Menard Electric Coop is menard.com, not the Menards retailer; Buckeye REC moved to buckeyerec.coop; Peru IN's utility site is peruutilities.com. Detailed tier is now 156. (3) Paperless: detailed entries with a paperless link rose from 50 of 128 (39%) to 98 of 156 (63%). Sources were the entries' own billing pages, sitemaps, and common paperless/SmartHub paths. The remaining gaps are mostly retail suppliers and JS-only co-op sites. Web search was unavailable (budget exhausted), so discovery relied on directories, the .gov list, domain probes and on-site navigation. || REVIEWER PASS 2 (2026-09-30, roster-backfill-electric-great-lakes): (a) Completeness: re-matched every OH/MI/IN/IL/WI row of rosters/electric_utilities.csv (EIA-861 2024) by utility ID; all are represented except the 3 non-residential rows already noted (University of Illinois, AGC Division of APGI, Ohio Valley Electric Corp). (c) Accuracy: HTTP-checked all 1,100+ link and website URLs on detailed entries (after retries all return 200 except 54 bot-blocked 403s on Westerville, Union Rural, Naperville, SCI REMC, Northeastern REMC, St. Charles, Columbus, CleanChoice and Batavia, which were browser-checked earlier). Phones corrected: Buckeye REC is now (800) 231-2732; Alger-Delta toll-free added. (d) Filled: CWLP AutoDebit/e-bill/history/mail address from its Account FAQs; Heartland REMC recurring-payment autopay; the City of Niles ACH form; CenterPoint 13-month history; and SmartHub history for one co-op. 30 detailed IOU/municipal/co-op entries had no assistance page on their own site, so they now link to their state program page, and the notes say so (Ohio HEAP/PIPP energyhelp.ohio.gov, Indiana EAP/LIHEAP at IHCDA, Illinois LIHEAP/PIPP at DCEO, Wisconsin WHEAP, Michigan MEAP at MPSC). Retail suppliers XOOM, Eligo and IDT were upgraded to detailed. Their notes say that in OH and IL their charges are on the utility's consolidated bill, so customers pay the utility. Detailed count is 161. Remaining gaps: 39 small municipals have no website, all under about 1,000 customers. Of the detailed entries, 52 lack a statements_history link and 60 lack a paperless link, mostly SmartHub co-ops whose public pages do not describe these. 28 lack a payment_processor (mostly retail suppliers). WebSearch was unavailable to this reviewer because the session's budget was exhausted, so discovery relied on member directories and domain probes. || REVIEWER PASS 3 (2026-09-30, roster-backfill-electric-great-lakes): (a) Correction: pass 2 said the remaining municipals without websites were all under about 1,000 customers; that was wrong. Tipton IN (4,294), Mascoutah IL (4,146), Lawrenceburg IN (3,769), Carmi IL (3,068), Clintonville WI (2,852), Flora IL (2,753) and Carlyle IL (2,080) were among them. [electric-mid-atlantic] Completeness checked against EIA-861 (2024) via rosters/electric_utilities.csv: every EIA-861 retail entity with state in NY, NJ, PA, DE, MD or DC appears (by eia_utility_id) either as a detailed entry or a roster entry - 24 IOU/state rows (all IOUs detailed; FirstEnergy Pennsylvania Electric Co. split into its four customer-facing brands Met-Ed, Penelec, Penn Power, West Penn Power; LIPA billed via PSEG Long Island), 24 cooperatives, 106 municipal systems, 148 retail power marketers (competitive suppliers, deduplicated across states), and 13 behind-the-meter solar providers. Detailed tier: all 25 investor-owned/state billers (Con Edison, O&R, Rockland Electric, PSE&G, JCP&L, ACE, PECO, PPL, Duquesne, Met-Ed, Penelec, Penn Power, West Penn, UGI Electric, Citizens', Wellsboro, Pike County L&P, BGE, Pepco, Delmarva, Potomac Edison, National Grid NY, NYSEG, RG&E, Central Hudson, PSEG Long Island); every co-op/muni with >25k customers (SMECO, Delaware Electric Coop, Choptank, Adams, Central Electric Coop, Vineland) except City of Dover DE (site unreachable from this environment - roster with website from DEMEC list); plus smaller co-ops/munis Valley REC, Claverack, Northwestern REC, United EC, Somerset REC, New Enterprise REC, Otsego EC, Easton Utilities, Hagerstown; and the 8 largest retail suppliers by in-scope customers (Constellation, Direct Energy, Inspire, CleanChoice, Energy Harbor, AEP Energy, Green Mountain, IGS). Roster websites for munis/co-ops were taken from state association member lists (MEUA NY, NYAPP, DEMEC, PREA) or confirmed by fetching the domain and matching the page title; roster entries marked verified=true only where the homepage was fetched this session; homepage-linked payment portals (Invoice Cloud, Municipal Online Payments, SmartHub) recorded as login_url. Key billing fact for seniors: in all six jurisdictions competitive suppliers are almost always billed on the utility's consolidated bill, so the payee is the utility (confirmed on Constellation, Direct Energy, Inspire and AEP Energy pages). No TVA distributors exist in this region. Known gaps: Fishers Island Utility (770 customers) and ~25 small PA boroughs have no confirmed website; Dover DE, Rockville Centre, Tri-County REC, Lewes BPW, Arcade, Andover blocked automated fetches; some utilities publish no public autopay-cancel instructions (autopay_cancel null); retail suppliers below the top 8 are roster-only with no website for most; Exelon/Con Ed statements pages require sign-in; community-solar subscription billers (NY/NJ/MD) and CCA/municipal aggregation programs are not enumerated; WebSearch quota was exhausted mid-task so second-pass verification of pay-by-phone numbers for some roster entries is still needed.

Accuracy pass: all 288 distinct URLs in the file were status-checked with curl (retrying failures one at a time); 284 resolved (200/202, or 403 to curl but read in the browser: tesla.com, shipleyenergy.com). 4 still failed: harborsideenergy.com and myaccount.reliant.com (connection refused), mothershipenergy.com (bot challenge, not bypassed) and texpoenergy.com (TLS certificate error); they were left in place with this caveat. Redirected URLs were updated (Frontier Utilities payment/FAQ pages moved under /help-center/; Discount Power guest pay moved to payment.discountpowertx.com). Content of 28 entries was re-read (curl text, WebFetch, or the built-in browser for script-rendered sites): WGL Energy (now verified - $10/remaining-month residential ETF), Shipley (now verified), NRG Home, Frontier, XOOM, Champion, Payless, Discount Power TX, Spark, Green Mountain, Just Energy, Tara, Amigo, Constellation, TXU, Gexa, 4Change, Rhythm, Southern Federal, Sunrun, EverBright, Dividend, Service Finance, GoodLeap, SunStrong, Energy Harbor, First Point Power, GoodCharlie. Filled autopay_cancel/paperless/payment_assistance where pages existed, pay-by-phone numbers (XOOM, Just Energy, Tara, Amigo), and approx_customers from EIA for Texas REPs and solar companies that had null. Utility-billed suppliers (most of the Mid-Atlantic/Great Lakes/New England entries) intentionally keep null autopay/statement links: the bill, autopay and history live at the utility, and each entry's notes say so. The web-search quota for this session was exhausted before the review started, so no new search-based discovery was possible; Summer Energy, Tomorrow Energy and OhmConnect remain unverified (sites parked/down).

[territories-utilities-gov] Checked against the territory rows of rosters/electric_utilities.csv (EIA-861: PREPA 1,511,847 customers; Guam Power Authority 53,559; VI WAPA 54,457; CNMI CUC 17,555; ASPA 12,684 - all five have detailed entries) and rosters/water_systems_large.csv (EPA SDWIS: every large PR system belongs to PRASA/AAA, Guam systems to GWA; CUC and ASPA provide water in CNMI/AS; WAPA provides potable water in the USVI), so every territory resident's electric and water biller is covered. Electric in PR: LUMA Energy bills all PREPA/AEE customers; Genera PR (New Fortress) only operates PREPA's legacy power plants and does not bill customers, so it has no entry. Behind-the-meter solar lessors in PR/GU/VI on EIA (Sunnova ~54k PR customers, Sunrun ~28k PR) bill separately for solar leases/PPAs but are out of scope here. Government: PR property tax (CRIM), PR income tax (Hacienda/SURI), PR marbete/driver services (CESCO/DTOP), Guam DRT income tax and real property tax (PayGuam), Guam vehicle registration renewal (MyGuamTax; the reviewer corrected an earlier pointer to myid.guam.gov, which is the driver's-license/ID portal), USVI BIR income tax, USVI Tax Collector property tax, USVI BMV, CNMI Division of Revenue and Taxation, American Samoa Tax Office. Propane: Tropigas and Empire Gas (PR) are detailed here and also appear as roster entries in propane-heating-oil.json. Not duplicated here because they exist elsewhere: AutoExpreso (PR tolls, dmv-tolls-municipal.json), Liberty Puerto Rico and Claro Puerto Rico (cable/internet/landline/wireless files), Triple-S and MCS (medicare-health-insurance.json); also already elsewhere: Viya and GTA/Teleguam, IT&E (CNMI), Bluesky (AS), Banco Popular/FirstBank PR, PR public housing and ASUME. Trash: Puerto Rico municipalities generally fund residential trash collection from municipal revenue (CRIM/IVU) and do not send separate household trash bills; USVI and CNMI likewise have no household trash bill found; ASPA bills solid waste on its combined utility bill; Guam Solid Waste Authority does bill about 20,000 curbside households monthly; the reviewer found its official site (gswa.guam.gov) and upgraded it to detailed. Limits this session: web search quota was exhausted partway through, so later research relied on direct fetches of official sites; several official pages render with JavaScript or refused automated fetch (GPA financial-assistance page 403, ADSEF site refused connection, guamtax.com contact page blank). Reviewer pass 2026-09-30: every URL in the file was status-checked with curl (all resolve; lumapr.com returns 403 and guamwaterworks.org returns 429 to curl, so those pages were re-read with a fetch tool). Page content was re-read for 25+ entries' links. Changes: GSWA upgraded from roster to detailed. Guam MVD entry corrected to the MyGuamTax renewal and verified. Guam DRT income-tax and RPT entries got phones, mailing address, the MyGuamTax 'How to pay your 1040' page and the Senior Citizen & Disability real property tax credit. CESCO URLs updated for the web.cescodigital.pr.gov redirect, and the marbete pay_bill now points to Hacienda's colecturía directory, which lists marbete renewal. AAA got its separate payment and correspondence PO boxes, CUC got a payment-arrangements link, and ASPA notes now cover the CashPower prepaid option. CNMI and American Samoa levy essentially no residential real property tax bill, so no property-tax entries exist for them. Web search was unavailable to the reviewer (quota exhausted), so new billers could be found only by probing official domains.

entries.mail_payment_address: Texas: XOOM Energy Texas, LLC, P.O. Box 660133, Dallas, TX 75266-0133; CA/GA: XOOM Energy [California|Georgia], LLC, Attn: Accounts Receivable, PO Box 650117, Dallas, TX 75265-0117
entries.payment_processor: Utility consolidated billing in most states; in-house for CA/GA/TX
entries.notes: Pay My Bill page (fetched 2026-09-30): 'If you receive your bill from your local utility company, you should continue to pay those bills directly to the utility'. How to Read Your Bill (fetched): sign up for AutoPay after logging in; most service areas use utility consolidated billing. Cancel Service page https://xoomenergy.com/en/cancel-account (fetched): term plans may carry an early termination (cost recovery) fee. Budget billing is utility-sponsored (not in IL or DC). Outside Texas, Georgia and California this supplier normally bills through the local utility (utility consolidated billing): the supply charge is a line on the utility bill, and the senior views, pays, sets up/cancels autopay and sees statement history in the utility's account (PSE&G, PECO, PPL, BGE, Pepco, ComEd, Ameren, AEP Ohio, FirstEnergy, Con Edison, National Grid, etc.). Call the supplier only about the rate, contract, renewal or cancellation. To return to the utility's default service, call the supplier or the utility; the switch takes 1-2 billing cycles. Fixed-rate contracts may carry an early termination fee (ETF) - check the contract summary. Utility-run help (LIHEAP, budget billing, senior/low-income discounts, PIPP/PCAP) still applies; in Ohio PIPP and some NY/PA/MD low-income customers cannot be served by a supplier. Reviewer-2 2026-10-01: Pay My Bill page (fetched): customers billed by their utility keep paying the utility; CA (SDG&E/SoCalGas), GA and TX customers pay XOOM online (MyXOOM), by phone, by mail or cash (TX: Barri, CheckFree, Fidelity Express; CA/GA: ACE, Walmart). 'Auto Bill Pay' is set up and changed in the billing system via MyXOOM > Pay My Bill (TX via the online billing portal) - same page reused for autopay setup/cancel. approx_customers = sum of EIA-861 2024 XOOM entities (~138,900; ~56,900 in TX).

entries.senior_programs: Electricity Lifeline Program (ELP, also called LIAP): bill credit of up to $1,200 per year for income-qualified customers, applied through Community Action agencies/MaineHousing (program year runs through Sept 30); Arrearage Management Program; SimplePay budget plan (/account/billingoptions/simplepay); Lifelight program (/support/lifelight) and medical-emergency disconnection protection for households with serious illness or life-sustaining equipment; 2-1-1 Maine referrals; winter disconnection rules (MPUC approval Nov 15-Apr 15).
entries.notes: cmpco.com blocks automated fetches; URLs from search results on the official domain. Pay Online: /account/waystopay/payonline (cmpco.com/paytoday); Pay by Mail: /account/waystopay/pay-by-mail; app: /account/waystopay/app. eBill lets you view up to 36 months of past bills. AutoPay: enroll online, in the app, or via form on back of bill stub; payment drafted ~23 days after bill mailed. No dedicated cancel page found. Reviewer (2026-09-29): cmpco.com still times out for live fetches, but Wayback Machine snapshots from Apr-Jun 2026 of /payment-and-billing-options, /account/waystopay/payonline and /account/waystopay/help-with-bill were read. They confirm: sign-in payment or Guest Payment (account number + bank info); AutoPay link goes to /payments/autopay/first-step (redirects into the portal.cmpco.com login, where AutoPay is enrolled and turned off); eBill shows up to 24 months of past bills (not 36 as earlier noted); pay by phone 800-750-4000 press 2; mail to Central Maine Power Company, P.O. Box 847810, Boston, MA 02284-7810; pay-in-person agencies (/account/waystopay/pay-in-person); payment text confirmations (text REG to 267898). Online card processor not named on the page. Kept verified=false because the live site could not be fetched.

Outside Texas, Georgia and California this supplier normally bills through the local utility (utility consolidated billing): the supply charge is a line on the utility bill, and the senior views, pays, sets up/cancels autopay and sees statement history in the utility's account (PSE&G, PECO, PPL, BGE, Pepco, ComEd, Ameren, AEP Ohio, FirstEnergy, Con Edison, National Grid, etc.). entries.name: Discount Power (Texas)
entries.notes: Homepage (fetched 2026-09-30): phone 1-877-455-4674; switch to another Discount Power plan within 90 days without an early termination fee. Not the same company as Discount Power Inc. (CT) - see separate entry. Texas REP: the REP sends its own bill (the TDU - Oncor, CenterPoint, AEP Texas, TNMP - only delivers). Low-income discounts are not available from the state; ask the REP for a payment extension or deferred payment plan, and call 2-1-1 for local assistance. Seniors 60+ can ask to be designated critically ill/chronic-condition or 'elderly' customers to get extra disconnection protections (PUCT rules). Reviewer 2026-09-30: Customer Care, FAQs and Read Your Bill pages (fetched): guest pay link on my.discountpowertx.com; automatic payment by card or bank draft; contract end date shown on statements; fixed-price plans may carry an early termination fee; renewal questions Mon-Fri 8-5 CST. NRG brand (the parent is per the TX regional file; Cirro/Discount Power/Pennywise share an entry there). Reviewer-2 2026-10-01: Guest-pay URL now redirects to payment.discountpowertx.com/public/guest-pay (updated). FAQs (WebFetch): register online to view all account details/billing; pays by check, bank draft or credit card; LITE-UP qualified customers can pay a deposit in 2 installments; no ETF on variable month-to-month plans, fixed plans may have a cancellation fee; 1-877-455-4674, service@discountpowertx.com. EIA reports Discount Power under US Retailers LLC (NRG; ~412,000 TX residential incl. Cirro Energy and Pennywise Power) - see electric-texas-mountain 'Cirro Energy / Discount Power / Pennywise Power' entry.
